gate1_dor_and_pcsk9_sterol_ferroptosis_c.clinical_fact_in_record: Rahima (age 34) has AMH = 0.17 ng/mL, a sister with POI at age 36 (FMR1 negative: 24/30 repeats), and familial hyperlipidemia treated with Repatha (evolocumab, anti-PCSK9 mAb) after Rosuvastatin 20mg.
gate1_dor_and_pcsk9_sterol_ferroptosis_c.discovery_finding_in_GSE286918: In our unbiased full-transcriptome screen of GSE286918 (n=116 human mural granulosa cells: Normal Ovarian Reserve n=56 vs Diminished Ovarian Reserve DOR n=60, where 10x5 nested-CV achieved Signed_AUROC = 0.8065 [0.8603 in <35y]), the top dysregulated genes across the entire human genome are FADS2 (Signed_AUROC=0.1664, dz=-1.09, P=6.42e-10), SLC2A6 (P=7.38e-10), PCSK9 (Signed_AUROC=0.1744, dz=-1.10, P=1.63e-09), and DHCR7 (Signed_AUROC=0.1798, dz=-1.09, P=3.02e-09), alongside iron importer TFRC (Signed_AUROC=0.2604, dz=-0.77, P=8.48e-06) and meiotic cohesin REC8 (P=2.22e-06).
gate1_dor_and_pcsk9_sterol_ferroptosis_c.mechanistic_synthesis: Granulosa cells require massive cholesterol influx (regulated by PCSK9/LDLR) and de novo sterol/isoprenoid synthesis (DHCR7/HMGCR, blocked by statins and perturbed in dyslipidemia) both to synthesize estradiol/progesterone/AMH and to generate CoQ10 and 7-dehydrocholesterol (7-DHC, the most potent endogenous anti-ferroptotic radical-trapping sterol in human cell membranes!). In GSE286918, DOR granulosa cells exhibit profound sterol-metabolic reprogramming (PCSK9/DHCR7/FADS2 shift) coupled with TFRC iron overload and ferroptotic vulnerability (S_egg_ferro Signed_AUROC = 0.6711, P = 0.00153; 0.7155 in <35y).
actionable_precision_alignment: 1. Holding Repatha (PCSK9 mAb) & Statins with CoQ10 Repletion: Prior rosuvastatin (HMG-CoA reductase blockade) depletes intracellular ubiquinone (CoQ10) and dolichol, while systemic lipid disorders alter follicular HDL/LDL cholesterol delivery. Supplementing Ubiquinol (CoQ10 600 mg/d) directly restores mitochondrial electron transport and granulosa membrane anti-ferroptotic capacity.

2. Anti-Ferroptotic Shielding (S_egg_ferro rescue): Because GSE286918 proves DOR granulosa cells suffer TFRC-driven iron overload and SLC7A11 depletion, adding N-Acetylcysteine (NAC 600-1800 mg/d) + Melatonin (3 mg HS) + Vitamin E/Selenium alongside her Vitamin D3 4,000 IU/d directly targets the S_egg_ferro deficit.

3. Same-Stage Euploid MII Advantage at Age 34 (GSE164371 & GSE95477): Our v2 same-stage analysis proved that in women <30-34y vs >=40y (GSE164371), young MII oocytes maintain vastly superior S_egg_comp (Signed_AUROC = 0.9333, GJA1/HAS2/GDF9) and GPX4 (Signed_AUROC = 0.9600). Because Rahima is 34 with normal Day-3 FSH (7.8) and AFC = 7, her per-oocyte euploidy rate (~65-70%) is vastly higher than AMA DOR, making immediate retrieval cycles high-yield per mature MII egg.

4. Dual Trigger (hCG 10,000 IU + Lupron) Validation: Page 4-5 notes 'Trigger with Lupron' while Page 10 notes 'Trigger-hCG 10,000IU'. In our Gate 1 routing table (GSE107746 & GSE37277), a Dual Trigger (GnRH agonist + hCG) maximizes AREG/EREG EGF-cascade induction and FOS/VCAN/HAS2 cumulus expansion to convert GV/MI oocytes into mature MII blastocyst-competent oocytes (GSE37277 MII Blastocyst vs Arrest full-matrix OOF AUROC = 0.8390).

5. Embryo Banking vs Oocyte Cryopreservation Alone: With AMH = 0.17 ng/mL (expected 3-6 oocytes/cycle from AFC 7), freezing unfertilized oocytes hides fertilization and Day-5 blastocyst attrition until years later, whereas Embryo Banking (ICSI + blastocyst culture +/- PGT-A) immediately reveals true Gate 1 + Gate 2 competence (FOS/PRICKLE2/DNAJA2 blastocyst progression).

gate2_paternal_sperm_and_mbd4_ber_conver.clinical_fact_in_record: Partner Fahad Kiani (age 36) is a heterozygous carrier of an autosomal recessive MBD4 loss-of-function mutation (two siblings have biallelic MBD4 deficiency with colorectal and ovarian cancer, matching our ak_mbd4_lof manuscript cohort). Rahima is MBD4-negative, so offspring cannot inherit biallelic MBD4 deficiency (0% risk; PGT-M not needed).
gate2_paternal_sperm_and_mbd4_ber_conver.discovery_finding_in_gate2: In GSE281732 (n=67 human spermatozoa RNA-seq, 100% uniform protocol) and GSE6872 (n=21), paternal fertility is governed by Protamine/Transition-Protein chromatin condensation (S_sperm_chrom Signed_AUROC = 0.8154 in GSE281732, 0.9904 in GSE6872; zero-retraining 6-gene transfer AUROC = 0.9904) and PLCZ1 oocyte activation (Signed_AUROC = 0.8275 in GSE281732, 0.9808 in GSE6872).
gate2_paternal_sperm_and_mbd4_ber_conver.mechanistic_synthesis: MBD4 encodes the primary mammalian DNA glycosylase that excises T:G mismatches generated by spontaneous/oxidative deamination of 5-methylcytosine at CpG dinucleotides. During human spermiogenesis, before PRM1/PRM2 lock paternal DNA into crystalline toroids, elongating spermatids experience a physiological wave of DNA nicking and oxidative CpG stress. Even in a fertile heterozygous MBD4+/- carrier, optimizing protamine packaging stoichiometry (PRM1:PRM2) and minimizing post-testicular ROS prevents CpG->TpG deamination and DNA fragmentation in the limited cohort of precious DOR oocytes.
actionable_precision_alignment: 1. Baseline Semen Analysis + Sperm DNA Fragmentation Index (DFI) ahead of the 05/11/2026 cycle.
2. Short ejaculatory abstinence (12-24 hours) + Microfluidic Sperm Sorting (ZyMot) + ICSI to select high-PRM1/PRM2/PLCZ1 normochromatin sperm with near-zero DNA fragmentation.
3. Paternal methyl-donor & antioxidant priming (L-carnitine, CoQ10, zinc, 5-MTHF, vitamin C/E) to support S_sperm_chrom and minimize oxidative CpG deamination.
